regressions.source: OAppPreCrimeSimulator.sol lzReceiveAndRevert: revert SimulationResult(abi.encode(...)) after preCrime.buildSimulationResult() (bytes argument)
regressions.issue: The bytes argument of the custom error, shown before as length, data and zero padding, is now one raw memory slice covering all three; the same build decodes the analogous 0x9a6d49cd revert better than before (32, _84, data, padding).
regressions.rule: Decode revert data word by word: a word known to equal n followed by n bytes copied from a source and zero padding prints as n, the source slice, Bytes(pad, 0), whatever the base expression of the buffer.

improvements: ecrecover's input decoded (sha3(0x1901, domainSeparator, structHash), v, r, s); sendCompose's composeMsg decoded as Array(len=..., data=Bytes(8, nonce), Bytes(4, srcEid), ...); quoteOFT's empty fee array returned as Array(len=0, data=''); string returns as Array(len=_32, ...); unknown functions' params named by calldata word (lzReceive: _param1, _param3.._param7; isComposeMsgSender: _param4, _param5), P6 3 -> 0; 107 fewer lines.
notes: Diff of 740 lines reviewed hunk by hunk on the substantive lines (calls, reverts, returns, logs; counts per function unchanged). permit and lzReceiveAndRevert drop free-pointer bumps and address their buffers from the unchanged mem[64] (e.g. ecrecover output read as mem[mem[64]] instead of mem[mem[64] - 32]): consistent within the text, the same pattern reported in c00063 and c00001.
summary: One minor regression: SimulationResult's bytes argument is now a single raw memory slice in its revert. Otherwise better: ecrecover input, compose message and empty arrays decoded, parameters named by calldata word.
